items.title: Codex MCP, hooks and live tool-catalog gate widened
items.summary: Codex main advanced 158 commits. The delta changes MCP catalog ownership/revision and refresh behavior, session hook refresh, permission/application requirements, thread lifecycle and app-server runtime. ctrl has no executable compatibility witness for the new policy/tool boundary.
items.localContractImpact: Keep the Codex hooks/tools/policy gate open; qualify the declared local policy and MCP execution boundary before adopting these runtime semantics.

observations.observation: Since 8e3b180d, Codex main changed MCP client-owned tool catalogs and refresh coordination, live app tool refresh, session-hook refresh, permissions/application requirements and thread/runtime behavior; no ctrl compatibility probe was executed.

claims.text: The changed Codex MCP/tool/policy boundary remains locally unqualified until the profile-declared executable gate runs.

items.title: Codex app-server protocol and generated schemas changed materially
items.summary: The 158-commit range modifies ClientRequest, ServerNotification, v2 thread, MCP, permissions, application requirements and generated JSON/TypeScript schemas. The alpha channel also advanced to the v0.153.4 line.
items.localContractImpact: Reconcile local app-server/config projections before treating current main/alpha as transport-compatible.

observations.observation: Generated and source protocol surfaces changed across request/notification, thread, MCP, permission and application-requirement types.

claims.text: The Codex protocol/schema/runtime projection differs materially from the prior admitted baseline.

items.title: CPython main fixes deeply nested inlined-comprehension compiler crash
items.summary: Forecast CPython main now includes gh-156091, fixing a crash compiling deeply nested inlined comprehensions. This is a compiler-semantic forecast, not the active 3.14 baseline.
items.localContractImpact: Track for future Python baseline migration and bind it to compiler probes; do not project it backward onto Python 3.14.

claims.text: The forecast compiler behavior changed and must remain distinct from the pinned active 3.14 runtime.

items.title: CUE master changes recursive-disjunction evaluator behavior
items.summary: CUE master advanced to eb886ed0 with an ADT scheduler fix that broadens bounded re-entry into recursive disjunctions. ctrl's pinned evaluator remains unchanged at 806821e4.
items.localContractImpact: Keep the current pin authoritative; require explicit evaluator migration qualification before adopting forecast master behavior.

observations.observation: Forecast evaluator semantics changed around recursive disjunction scheduling/re-entry; pinned evaluator identity did not change.

claims.text: CUE master is migration evidence only and cannot replace the pinned evaluator without profile qualification.

items.localContractImpact: Verify schema/binding compatibility before updating any SCIP identity consumer; do not treat SCIP identity as runtime truth.

claims.text: The SCIP identity/interface surface advanced and requires compatibility correlation before local adoption.

items.title: GenAI Python instrumentation now records cancellation as failure
items.summary: The Python GenAI implementation changed cancellation handling so BaseException cancellation paths produce failure/error observations rather than success-like UNSET status.
items.localContractImpact: Account for the changed observation semantics in future telemetry correlation; telemetry remains observation-only.

observations.observation: Cancellation and other BaseException paths are now recorded through fail(), changing emitted error/status evidence.

claims.text: GenAI cancellation telemetry changed, but it remains execution observation rather than qualification authority.
